title: Buddha Ram v. U.P. Power Corporation
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Ashok Bhushan, J.; Naheed Ara Moonis, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; petitioner relegated to Supply Code, 2005 remedies.
headnote: A writ of mandamus to compel the licensee to decide a consumer's application against disconnection and alleged wrong bills cannot be entertained. The consumer must take the appropriate remedy under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Buddha Ram, a consumer, filed Writ-C No. 45710 of 2011 against U.P. Power Corporation and others. He sought a mandamus directing the respondents to decide his application dated 18 July 2011. The application alleged disconnection of electric supply on 3 April 2011 and asked for a decision on wrong bills issued to him. The Division Bench of Ashok Bhushan and Naheed Ara Moonis, JJ. heard counsel for both sides on 11 August 2011.

holding_units.holding: Where a consumer seeks a mandamus to decide an application alleging disconnection and wrong bills, the writ is not entertainable; the consumer must take the appropriate remedy under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
holding_units.flag: order cites the Supply Code generally, without a clause number

not_decided.point: Whether the 3 April 2011 disconnection was illegal and whether the bills were wrong
not_decided.note: The Court did not examine the disconnection or the bills on merits.
